design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST: an Original Medicare CGM user whose insulin treatment ended asks to sign the Medicare form so sensors keep coming. The agent must see that the notice's units depend on an unrecorded renewal order (prerequisite, state form), record that grant with a six-factor count (span anchored past the still-valid previous grant, a per-shipment quantity read as 1 per 30 days, a coverage-review length of the follow-up interval because the insulin supply ended (cross insulin), the treating prescriber's visit, the regimen-change date from the testing-supplies order (cross bgm), and a bridge block for the refill due before the counted span), then size the notice with five factors (drawn authorization, exposure-limited delivery, listed basis, coverage risk scope, prior-notice credit). Difficulty comes from reading policy and reconciling 24 ledger rows, 11 order/authorization/visit rows, 16 shipment rows and two other programs.
SCOPE: task 0 claims cgm_ext_renewal_authorization_units (record_order_authorization_630fe26e, agent) and cgm_ext_medicare_advance_notice_units (sign_medicare_advance_notice_77a558d1, user). Reserved for task 1 (PPO, a Tandem Mobi pump forces a Libre 2 Plus -> Dexcom G7 change): authorization grant for the model-change order under the payer PA in force, plan member waiver, payment plan, sensor refill - disjoint events and tools.
DRAW: draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems 1, factor_counts [5, 6]; grant takes 6, notice takes 5.
PROBLEM TREE: root = notice (on_request, owner user). Edge notice -> grant: value_input, gate drawn_units_left, form state, sentence 'The units the advance notice lists are fixed only after every written order on file for the item stands recorded as an authorization grant.' (affirmative 'only after'; names a record-visible state; no tool/id; exactly the renewal grant write brings it about because only an authorization grant row resting on the order satisfies it). Seed falsifies it: renewal order da4565f8-fc45-4d99-854f-38ff09d187a0 has no grant; GR-B exhausted. Deletion run: notice 1 -> 0 without the grant.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: grant step - written_order_on_file (renewal order names item A4239, quantity, date, NPI 1124690372) and initial_visit_on_file (not the program's first grant; initial-qualification visit 2022-12-12 on file) both hold. Notice step - customer_signs is retired by a declared overwrite because that caller-statement gate binds the internal enrollment reference no customer can state; the replaced_by keeps 'signs personally ... no representative can sign' and evidences it by her own recorded signing call. No time gates on either subject.
OVERWRITES: grant - base 'records the authorization grant itself ... for the billing units the order covers within that span' is replaced for renewals on this tier only (keeps basis, valid-from and valid-through). Notice - base billable-after-signing clause extended to coverage-in-doubt supplies on Original Medicare only, with the commercial plan member waiver case of task 1 excluded by name; signing clause as above.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: renewal order da4565f8-fc45-4d99-854f-38ff09d187a0 (2026-10-08..2027-10-07, qty 3); GR-B e4b6c126-2aec-44cc-9e0e-a8cc43849c12 (12 units, all drawn by the four refills 2025-12-04..2026-08-03); latest refill drew on GR-B; ABN of 2026-09-18 (1 unit) credited; billing nets to 0.00.
FACTOR CARD (grant, recomputed): span_start_anchor (method): grant GR-B valid 2025-12-03..2026-12-02 is still valid on order date 2026-10-08 -> blocks counted 2026-12-03..2027-10-07 = 309 days = 10 blocks, anchor 2026-12-02; baseline (order date, 365 days = 12 blocks, anchor 2026-10-08) gives 6. | order_quantity_convention (method): renewal order states 3 per 30 days = allowance 1 x 3 blocks of a 90-day shipment -> 1 unit per block; baseline (as written, 3) gives 12. | coverage_review_length (parameter, cross insulin): latest insulin fill 2026-06-29 + 90 days ended 2026-09-27, on or before the order date 2026-10-08, and the pharmacy closed 2026-08-05 (2 months before the order date, under the 6-month interval) -> review length 6 months; baseline (standard review length, the 3 blocks of one standard shipment) gives 1. | review_visit_practitioner (method): treating prescriber 1124583907 has 4 qualifying visits, latest 2026-07-20; baseline (any practitioner: the 2026-09-14 visit by NPI 1124712058) gives 5. | regimen_change_record (parameter, cross bgm): testing-supplies program treatment class non_insulin_treated, newest written order 2026-08-12 -> regimen change date 2026-08-12; baseline (standard regimen change date, the latest insulin refill's ship date 2026-06-29) gives 3. | refill_bridge (parameter): GR-B has 0 units left; next refill 2026-08-03 + 90 - 10 = 2026-10-22 falls before 2026-12-02 -> blocks 2026-10-22..2026-12-02 = 42 days = 1 block; baseline (no bridge) gives 3. | plain: review start = later of 2026-07-20 and 2026-08-12 = 2026-08-12; months left = 6 - MONTHS(2026-08-12, 2026-12-02)=3 -> 3; counted blocks = min(10, 3) = 3; result = 1 x (3 + 1) = 4.
FACTOR CARD (notice, recomputed on the post-grant world): drawn_authorization (method): latest refill (2026-08-03) drew on GR-B which has 0 units left; the renewal grant (valid 2026-10-08..2027-10-07, 4 units) is valid on the next delivery date 2026-10-22 -> draws on it; baseline (GR-B, 0 left) gives 0. | exposure_limited_delivery (parameter): program balance 0.00 (24 ledger postings net to zero) and the testing-supplies program is active -> 2 blocks; baseline (standard 3 blocks) gives 2. | listed_delivery_basis (method): latest refill carries confirmation date 2026-08-01 -> lists the next delivery = min(2 blocks, 11 blocks to 2027-10-07, 4 units left) x 1 = 2; baseline (one standard shipment = 3) gives 2. | coverage_risk_scope (method, cross insulin): insulin pharmacy closed, latest insulin supply ended 2026-09-27 before 2026-10-22 -> every listed unit at risk (2); baseline (none at risk) gives 0. | prior_notice_credit (parameter): ABN of 2026-09-18 for 1 unit signed after the 2026-08-03 refill and after the 2026-08-05 closure -> 1 credited; baseline (none) gives 2. | plain: result = max(0, 2 - 1) = 1.
PARAMETER NOTE: regimen_change_record selects a date (testing-supplies order 2026-08-12 / testing-supplies activation date / standard: latest insulin refill ship date) and is declared a parameter factor. METHOD-TIER PAIRWISE TABLE: span anchor a/b/c differ by whether a grant is valid on the order date and whether the latest supply runs past it (a gives 309 days here, c 365); quantity convention a (divide per-shipment count) vs c (as written) differ on quantity 3; b holds at 0 and differs from both; visit practitioner a vs c differ when a later visit by another NPI exists (2026-09-14); drawn authorization a/b/c give newest grant / nothing / previous grant; listed basis a/b/c give next delivery (2) / units left (4) / standard shipment (3); risk scope a/b/c give all / all less one block / none.
FACTOR INDEPENDENCE (transitive read check, run on the charter): no factor binding reads another factor's binding directly or through plain bindings; 'the customer has stopped insulin' (insulin_stopped) is one plain binding stated once in each rule and read by the standard coverage review of the renewal and by coverage_risk_scope and prior_notice_credit; shared reads (order dates, previous grant, latest refill, insulin status) are plain bindings and the result bindings assemble them.
CLOSURE-REASON CARD: the insulin tests (the renewal's standard coverage review, coverage_risk_scope, prior_notice_credit anchor) test closure_reason customer_discontinued, not the status alone; this world's insulin program closed 2026-08-05 as customer_discontinued and the persona confirms she stopped insulin, so the tiers taken are unchanged. NOTICE TYPE: the prior-notice credit reads only notices of type abn_cms_r_131 (the 2026-09-18 notice is one). CROSS: exposure_limited_delivery reads the testing-supplies program and is declared cross_difficulty bgm. MONTHS CONVENTION: the coverage review months left and the notice credit's window count whole calendar months as each rule now states (calendar-month difference, less one when the later date's calendar day is earlier), matching the compute; values unchanged. ROUND-8 ORDER CARD (N8): the renewal's result sentence fixes the order generically - replacements first (span blocks and anchor as replaced), then the coverage-review limit on the span's blocks so replaced counting to the replaced anchor, then blocks added on top of the span, which the limit does not reach. Readings excluded by the text: (B) a limit over the added bridge too, min(10 + 1, 3) = 3, is excluded because added blocks 'are not limited by the coverage review'; (C) the replacement lifting the limit, 10 + 1 = 11, is excluded because the limit 'is then applied to the span's blocks so replaced'. Only the compute's min(10, 3) + 1 = 4 remains. The advance notice states its order the same way (grant, supply blocks and listing replaced, then the payment expectation on the listed units, units taken off last). ROUND-7 XF CARD: every rule is now a standard-method paragraph in record terms (baseline.rule names no factor quantity or zero default), shared plain quantities defined once, self-contained adjustment sentences that say how they change the standard amount, and one generic result sentence. Renewal: the coverage review (stopped insulin and a documented insulin regimen) is part of the standard grant with its standard review length (one standard shipment's 3 blocks), review visit (latest qualifying visit by any practitioner) and regimen change date (latest insulin refill ship date); the review-length, review-visit and regimen-change adjustments replace those standard figures; all-baseline 9. Advance notice: standard next delivery and listing, Medicare expected to pay every listed unit; the stopped-without-closed-date case gets no credit by its own sentence; next-delivery units now compare units with units (blocks times the allowance). Mechanical check: cgm_ext_renewal_authorization_units: non-factor/baseline factor-term hits=none; result hits=none; factor-reads-factor=none | cgm_ext_medicare_advance_notice_units: non-factor/baseline factor-term hits=none; result hits=none; factor-reads-factor=none | cgm_ext_model_change_authorization_units: non-factor/baseline factor-term hits=none; result hits=none; factor-reads-factor=none | cgm_ext_plan_member_waiver_units: non-factor/baseline factor-term hits=none; result hits=none; factor-reads-factor=none | cgm_ext_payment_plan_installment: non-factor/baseline factor-term hits=none; result hits=none; factor-reads-factor=none | cgm_ext_model_change_refill_units: non-factor/baseline factor-term hits=none; result hits=none; factor-reads-factor=none. ROUND-5 SOURCE CARD: the advance notice's signature overwrite now keeps every other notice under the base rule (personal signature, no representative signing); the waiver is named by its general subject; the next delivery's newest grant is the one with the latest valid-through date; the exposure rule sizes the next delivery without naming risk; the credit applies only when the customer has stopped insulin; an insulin program without refills counts as a supply that has ended; the renewal states its no-refill, no-visit and review-after-anchor cases (months counted as zero), and its assembly sentence alone combines the factor outputs; transitive read check: no violation. EDGE PROBES: no insulin refill on record -> review length = interval and standard regimen date earlier than every record / every listed unit at risk; no qualifying visit -> the review visit counts as earlier than every record and the review starts on the regimen change date (all visits removed: bgm order 2026-08-12 -> 4 units; bgm removed, standard regimen date = latest insulin refill 2026-06-29 -> 2 units); insulin closed as changed_supplier -> no coverage review -> 11 units; pharmacy closed 7 months before the order date -> review length 0 -> 1 unit (bridge only); ABSENT-RECORD SWEEP: the no-refill, no-insulin-refill, no-visit and review-after-anchor sentences each state the binding's result with every other input of the same binding (regimen date, stopped-insulin test, grant validity) unchanged, as the compute evaluates; review start after the anchor -> zero months elapsed; insulin program closed as changed_supplier -> no coverage review, no units at risk, no credit anchor; a plan member waiver or other non-ABN notice on file -> never credited; no previous grant -> previous_valid_through '0000-00-00', tier c; no refill -> refill date defaults, no bridge; no insulin program -> no coverage review, risk none; no bgm program -> standard regimen date (latest insulin refill ship date, or earlier than every record); second open notice older than the latest refill -> tier b credit only beyond that refill's units; zero-division none (blocks_per_shipment >= 1).
PERSONA: calm retired librarian; volunteers only the goal (sign the Medicare form so sensors continue), phone 6145550117, DOB 1953-08-27, ZIP 43123; facts on request (still wearing, two weeks left, insulin stopped August, September form); passive hold if something must be set up; signs exactly what she is handed; closes when told it is recorded.
STANDARD SOLUTION: locate, verify, read program/orders/shipments/billing/insulin/bgm, record grant (4 units, 2026-10-08..2027-10-07, A4239, renewal order), hand the notice; customer signs 1 unit of A4239.
VERIFICATION: /tmp authoring harness reproducing check_compute bindings gave grant=4 (baseline 36) and notice=1 (baseline 0); gates run per task are recorded below.
user_scenario: You are Philippa Quarshie-Lindgren, 73, a retired school librarian in Grove City, Ohio, who wears a Dexcom G7 that Larkfield Medical Supply ships you every three months under Original Medicare. Over the summer your endocrinologist took you off your nightly basal insulin and moved you to a once-weekly injection, and you still check your sugar with your Contour Next One meter, whose strips also come from Larkfield. A friend told you Medicare might stop paying for CGM sensors once you are not on insulin, and your next box of sensors should be due in about a week. You are calling to find out what you have to sign so the sensors keep coming even if Medicare refuses to pay; you would rather pay for them yourself than go without, and you want to sign the Medicare form today. When the representative asks how to find your account you give the phone number on file, 6145550117; to confirm who you are you give your date of birth, 1953-08-27, and your ZIP code, 43123, and you offer your email pquarshie.lindgren@larkspurmail.net only if they still need another detail. You answer other questions only when asked: you are still wearing the Dexcom every day and have roughly two weeks of sensors left; your last insulin pens came at the end of June and you stopped the insulin in early August; you have not been in a hospital or nursing facility; back in September someone from Larkfield had you sign a Medicare form for one box; you do not know of any unpaid bill; your only coverage is Medicare Part B plus your drug plan. If the representative says something has to be updated on their side first, you are glad to hold while they do it. When the representative hands you the Medicare notice to sign and tells you the enrollment reference, the item and the number of units, you sign it exactly as they give it and ask them to read back what you signed. You do not know Medicare's rules or how many units the form should list; if a number sounds odd to you, you only ask them to double-check it against your records, without suggesting a figure. Once they tell you the notice is signed and recorded, you thank them and say goodbye.

coverage_review_length (parameter, cross insulin): latest insulin fill 2026-06-29 + 90 days ended 2026-09-27, on or before the order date 2026-10-08, and the pharmacy closed 2026-08-05 (2 months before the order date, under the 6-month interval) -> review length 6 months; baseline (standard review length, the 3 blocks of one standard shipment) gives 1.
review_visit_practitioner (method): treating prescriber 1124583907 has 4 qualifying visits, latest 2026-07-20; baseline (any practitioner: the 2026-09-14 visit by NPI 1124712058) gives 5.

regimen_change_record (parameter, cross bgm): testing-supplies program treatment class non_insulin_treated, newest written order 2026-08-12 -> regimen change date 2026-08-12; baseline (standard regimen change date, the latest insulin refill's ship date 2026-06-29) gives 3.

refill_bridge (parameter): GR-B has 0 units left; next refill 2026-08-03 + 90 - 10 = 2026-10-22 falls before 2026-12-02 -> blocks 2026-10-22..2026-12-02 = 42 days = 1 block; baseline (no bridge) gives 3.

plain (standard coverage review, the customer stopped insulin and the program documents basal_insulin_only): review start = later of 2026-07-20 and 2026-08-12 = 2026-08-12; months left = 6 - MONTHS(2026-08-12, 2026-12-02)=3 -> 3; counted blocks = min(10, 3) = 3; result = 1 x (3 + 1) = 4.

edges.condition: Every cgm_order_receipt row of item A4239 on the program has a cgm_authorization_grant row whose related_cgm_order_id is that order.
edges.policy_source: The units the advance notice lists are fixed only after every written order on file for the item stands recorded as an authorization grant.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The renewal written order of 2026-10-08 is on file but no authorization grant rests on it, so the newest grant is GR-B with no units left.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The authorization write creates a cgm_authorization_grant row with related_cgm_order_id = the renewal order, valid 2026-10-08..2027-10-07 with 4 units; drawn_units_left on the next delivery becomes 4 and the notice lists 2 at-risk units.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge: the notice waits on the renewal grant; no parallel prerequisites, so no second order exists.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the authorization write leaves the next delivery drawing on GR-B with 0 units left: notice_units becomes 0 instead of 1, and the terminal DB lacks the renewal grant.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions the renewal order, an authorization or any setup step; the only related line is a passive 'if the representative says something has to be updated on their side first, you are glad to hold'.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: sign_medicare_advance_notice_77a558d1 creates the notice row with whatever units it receives and never reads grants; record_order_authorization_630fe26e writes the grant without checking orders, visits or insulin status.
